title: Fix debanding for Mobile rendering method with HDR 2D.
body: Fixes #108757 In addition to fixing the bug, this PR aligns the dither to the appropriate data format (8 bit or 10 bit) to reduce both banding/ringing and noise. I've also removed a duplicate `convert_to_srgb` conditional statement from `renderer_compositor_rd.cpp` because this conditional is also performed in `blit.glsl`. I think it's better to have the conditional check only occur in a single place, since it makes things confusion when editing the code and seeing no change in behaviour. There are a few places where I've made assumptions about the `DataFormat` of the Framebuffer: I've noted these assumptions as comments so that if any issues arise in the future it will be easier to track down where the bad assumption is being made. If my code is correct, debanding will be applied any time floating point values need to be quantized to integer values. For example, if a 10-bit integer buffer is loaded into shader-land as floats and then modified (for example, by applying a glow, tonemapping, or transfer function), then it needs to be benanded before being written back to a 10-bit buffer. Additionally, any time color data is transformed from 10-bit to 8-bit, debanding will need to be applied again. The only time when debanding is not needed is when an image is read from an integer data format and written to an integer data format of the same bit depth without any floating point transformations on the image. In this case, if debanding was applied it should have no effect on the image because the debanding function is designed to apply noise/grain 50% above and below the colour value in the destination data format -- if the color is already perfectly aligned to the buffer's data format like in this case, then the 50% above and below will simply round back to the same color data as the original image. ...Unfortunately, it seems that rounding doesn't work exactly this way with my drivers. I suspect that rounding behaviour is simply not standardized and guaranteed. With my drivers, I need to modify the dither function as follows to get no rounding error and therefore no additional noise when applying the dither function to an already-quantized image: ``` vec3 dither = vec3(dot(vec2(171.0, 231.0), frag_coord)); dither.rgb = fract(dither.rgb / vec3(103.0, 71.0, 97.0)); dither = (dither.rgb - 0.5); dither = max(dither, -0.43); return dither / 255.0; ``` or: ``` vec3 dither = vec3(dot(vec2(171.0, 231.0), frag_coord)); dither.rgb = fract(dither.rgb / vec3(103.0, 71.0, 97.0)); return (dither.rgb - 0.5) * 0.86 / 255.0; ``` But with different drivers, a different "dither strength" modifier might be needed to produce stable rounding behaviour. All that to say, it's good to disable the debanding in these scenarios to ensure we don't get any extra noise when debanding should be producing no difference to the image. | 4.4.1 | `master` | This PR | --- | --- | --- | | | Mobile Without | Mobile With Debanding -- | -- | | Forward+ Without Debanding | Forward+ With Debanding -- | -- | | In addition to fixing the bug, this PR aligns the dither to the appropriate data format (8 bit or 10 bit) to reduce both banding/ringing and noise.
